entities.summary:
John Cantius (Jan z Kęt, 1390–1474), a towering figure in late medieval Central European intellectual and spiritual life, was a Polish Catholic priest, scholastic philosopher, physicist, and theologian whose career unfolded primarily at the Kraków Academy (later Jagiellonian University). Born in Kęty, Poland, his life spanned a period of significant intellectual ferment and religious devotion, positioning him as a key exponent of Aristotelian thought and a model of Christian erudition. His enduring significance lies in his rigorous academic contributions, his meticulous work in preserving and transmitting knowledge, and his profound personal piety that eventually led to his canonization.

Cantius dedicated over four decades to teaching philosophy and theology at the Kraków Academy, where he earned a reputation for both his intellectual depth and his humility. He lectured extensively on Aristotle's *Physics* and *Metaphysics*, integrating classical thought with Christian doctrine, and meticulously copied and corrected numerous manuscripts, thereby playing a crucial role in the dissemination of knowledge during an era preceding widespread printing. Beyond academia, he served as a parish priest in Olkusz for a period and undertook four pilgrimages on foot to Rome, demonstrating a profound personal faith that complemented his scholarly pursuits. His academic rigor was matched by a commitment to asceticism and charity, often distributing his earnings to the poor.
